# Row-level error diagnosis (executor X)

**Provenance.** Run `zeroshot500_qwen35_4b_img_only_native_4c17aa3__raw_500` (Qwen3.5-4B image-only, keyed JSON), generated by `uv run python scripts/row_error_diagnosis.py` (repo state `139186f+dirty`; ORACLE bootstrap 2000 doc-level paired resamples, seed 42). Every number is computed from the run's `predictions.json` / `trace.jsonl`, the gold labels, the OCR cache and the unmodified official scorer (`assignment/score.py` via `shipdoc.eval`). **All numbers UNVERIFIED** until a verifier recomputes them. Aggregates and counts only: no gold or predicted values, no names; value-level examples are in the local, outside-repo `<SHIPDOC_RUNS_DIR>/diagnosis/row_errors_local.md`.

### X1.1 Breakdown (unpaired rows / all rows of the bucket)

`page position`: `only` = single-page doc, `first` / `middle` / `last` = page of a multipage doc (`middle` = a continuation page that is not the last). Scorer-paired invoice rows (full + partial pairs) with a customer_part_number / purchase_order null-status mismatch: 386. Kinds: `po_in_cpn_slot` = gold cpn empty, predicted cpn equals the gold PO, predicted PO empty; `cpn_false_fill` / `po_false_fill` = gold empty, prediction filled; `cpn_over_null` / `po_over_null` = gold filled, prediction empty; `mixed` = both fields differ in null status in another way.

`po_in_cpn_slot` rows: 278 (66 scanned, 212 digital) in 4 groups (inv_g05, inv_g12, inv_g17, inv_g18); groups whose gold layout prints NO customer-part column: 4 of 4; groups whose layout prints a PO column: 4 of 4; rows in a group without a customer-part column: 278 of 278. In these groups there is no customer-part column to read, so the model fills a column that does not exist: it writes the PO value into the cpn slot and leaves the PO slot empty.

Groups with the SAME layout class (PO column, no customer-part column) in dev and no `po_in_cpn_slot` row: inv_g06 (inv_g06: 341 paired rows). So the missing customer-part column is necessary-looking but NOT sufficient: the error is concentrated in the groups listed above.

Mixed groups (column printed on some rows only): 0.

Format shapes (digits -> 9, letters -> A) in the TRAIN gold: 2 cpn shapes, 2 PO shapes, 0 shared; 2 cpn-only and 2 PO-only shapes (basis of candidate rule R3).

## X4. Cause -> fix class -> ORACLE recoverable points

ORACLE replay (**ORACLE upper bound, not achievable**): the rows / cells of the cause are replaced by gold (pairs: the predicted row becomes the gold row; gold-only rows are appended; predicted-only rows are removed; slot mismatches get the gold cpn / po; waybill over-nulls get the gold value), then the unmodified scorer rescores the 100 dev docs. Delta = OVERALL points vs the run's 83.86; CI = paired doc-level bootstrap (2000 resamples, seed 42). Effects are NOT additive (OVERALL is a mean of per-doc scores and row F1 is a ratio); the combined rows are computed, not summed. Causes with zero rows are listed in X1.3 and have no ORACLE row.

| cause | n rows / cells | scanned / digital | fix class | recoverable OVERALL points [95% CI] (ORACLE upper bound, not achievable) | confidence in the classification |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| rows: spn_copies_other_slot | 17 gold / 17 pred (2 docs) | 17 / 0 | fine-tune target (single doc; the gold part number is in the OCR text) | +0.14 [+0.00, +0.36] | low: one doc, mechanism unknown |
| rows: column_shift | 261 gold / 261 pred (38 docs) | 102 / 159 | multi-page context strategy (column order of page 1 given to continuation pages) + fine-tune target (continuation-page rows) | +2.88 [+1.85, +4.05] | medium: most shifts sit on header-less continuation pages and the contrast holds inside supplier groups, but 7 docs, 13 shifts sit on pages with a header row, and the mechanism (missing column header) is inferred from OCR layout, not seen |

Sum of the 11 single-cause deltas above = +12.30 pts vs the combined ORACLE +13.54 pts: the gap (+1.24) is the non-additivity (a doc's OVERALL has a fully-correct component, so fixing the last wrong cell of a doc is worth more than its cell share).

### Candidate merge-rule replays (achieved on dev, unmodified scorer, NOT oracles)

Four rules that follow from the findings above, replayed one at a time on the run's predictions. They are NOT upper bounds: they use only the model output, the OCR text and (R3) format shapes learned from TRAIN gold. R1 and R2 were designed after looking at the dev over-nulls, so their dev numbers are optimistic; R2's precision is also checked on all train+dev waybills in X3. `touched` = cells / rows the rule changed; `fixed` = wrong before, right after; `broken` = right before, wrong after.

| rule | touched | fixed | broken | wrong after | d OVERALL pts [95% CI] | d row F1 pts | d header acc pts |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| R1 waybill carrier <- own supplier_name slot | 7 | 7 | 0 | 0 | +0.23 [+0.06, +0.46] | +0.00 | +0.17 |
| R2 waybill mawb / hawb <- unique OCR pattern match | 41 | 41 | 0 | 0 | +1.44 [+0.92, +1.97] | +0.00 | +1.00 |
| R3 cpn <-> po slot swap by format shape (shapes from train gold) | 287 | 278 | 0 | 9 | +2.86 [+1.81, +3.99] | +5.64 | +0.00 |
| R4 part number <- nearest OCR span when absent from OCR | 249 | 92 | 140 | 156 | -1.23 [-1.98, -0.44] | -0.77 | +0.00 |

Mechanisms (one line per cause):

- `spn_misread`: the part number is the right line read with 1-2 wrong characters (see the edit profile in X1.3); the model, not the OCR layout, is the weak reader here and the OCR text is wrong too in a part of the cases, so snapping to it breaks as many rows as it fixes.
- `column_shift`: cpn / po / part-number values land one slot to the left or right; concentrated on continuation pages that carry no column-header row, where the model has to guess the column order.
- `spn_copies_other_slot`: the part-number slot is filled with the PO value of the same row (one doc, 17 rows), although the gold part number is readable in the OCR text.
- `page_short`: a page yields fewer rows than the gold page holds (one doc).
- `slot:po_in_cpn_slot`: layouts without a customer-part column: the PO value is written into the customer_part_number slot and purchase_order is left empty.
- `header:mawb`: the model emits a null mawb although MAWB value and label are on the page and in the OCR text; mostly scanned pages.
- `header:carrier`: the carrier is the letterhead company name (no 'carrier' label on any waybill); the model writes it into the invoice-schema supplier_name slot, which the merge drops.
- `header:hawb`: the model emits a null hawb although value and label are in the OCR text (scanned pages).
